question: In a v–t graph, if the slope keeps changing, it means:
solution:
The correct answer is __**acceleration is non-uniform**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **v–t graph** (Velocity-Time graph), the **slope** of the line represents the **acceleration** of the moving object.
 
• If the **slope keeps changing** at different points on the graph, it indicates that the **rate of change of velocity** is not constant over **time**. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Uniform acceleration** is represented by a **straight line** with a **constant slope**, meaning the **velocity** increases or decreases by equal amounts in equal intervals of **time**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• If the **speed is constant**, the **velocity** does not change, resulting in a **slope of zero**. This is represented by a **horizontal straight line** parallel to the **time axis**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• The **displacement** of an object is calculated by the **area under the curve** of a **v–t graph**. A changing slope describes how the **velocity** is changing, but it does not imply that the **displacement** is **zero**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is acceleration is non-uniform.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration:**
 
 
• It is a **vector quantity** defined as the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to **time**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **acceleration** is **m/s²** (meters per second squared).
 
• **Non-uniform acceleration** occurs when an object's **velocity** changes by **unequal amounts** in **equal intervals of time**, resulting in a **curved line** on a **v–t graph**.
 
 
 
• **Graph Interpretations:**
 
 
• In a **Distance-Time graph**, the **slope** represents **speed**.
 
• In a **Displacement-Time graph**, the **slope** represents **velocity**.
 
• In a **Velocity-Time graph**, a **positive slope** indicates **acceleration**, while a **negative slope** indicates **retardation** or **deceleration**.
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• For **uniform acceleration**, the three **kinematic equations** used are **v = u + at**, **s = ut + 1/2at²**, and **v² = u² + 2as**, where **u** is **initial velocity** and **v** is **final velocity**.
 
• These equations cannot be directly applied to **non-uniform acceleration**; instead, **calculus** (differentiation and integration) is required.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Instantaneous Acceleration:** When the **slope** of a **v–t graph** is **changing**, the **acceleration** at any **specific second** is called **instantaneous acceleration**, which is the **slope of the tangent** at that point.
 
• **Zero Acceleration:** This occurs when an object moves with **constant velocity**. The **v–t graph** is a **flat line**, and the **slope** is **0**.
 
• **Area Calculation:** To find the **total distance** traveled from a **v–t graph**, one must calculate the **magnitude** of the **area** between the curve and the **time axis**.
 
• **Real-world Examples:** A **car driving through heavy traffic** or a **bus stopping at intervals** are classic examples of **non-uniform acceleration**, where the **v–t graph** would show a **continuously changing slope**.
